sections.skill: Calculate gross pay for hourly work, including overtime

questions.prompt: Jada earns $16.50 per hour and works 24 hours this week. What is her gross pay for the week?
questions.intro: An hourly wage is the amount paid for each hour of work. Gross pay is the total earned before taxes or any other deductions are taken out. For hourly work: gross pay = hourly wage × hours worked.

misconceptions.A: Adds the wage and the hours

sources: U.S. Department of Labor: Under the FLSA, covered nonexempt employees receive overtime pay of at least 1.5 times the regular rate for hours over 40 in a workweek; some states set a higher minimum wage than the federal one. (https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime)

IRS (Publication 531): Employees who receive $20 or more in cash and charged tips in a month from one employer must report them to that employer; all tips, including noncash tips, are income. (https://www.irs.gov/publications/p531)

IRS (No tax on tips deduction): A new deduction for qualified tips (tax years 2025-2028, with limits) lowers income tax only; tips still must be reported, and Social Security and Medicare taxes still apply. (https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/what-the-no-tax-on-tips-deduction-means-for-you)

questions.prompt: Malik is a covered, nonexempt hourly employee who earns $18 per hour. He works 46 hours in one workweek. Under the federal overtime rule, what is his gross pay?
questions.intro: Federal law (the Fair Labor Standards Act) requires covered, nonexempt employees to be paid at least 1.5 times their regular rate for hours over 40 in a workweek: "time and a half." Hours up to 40 are paid at the regular rate. Some jobs are exempt from overtime.

misconceptions.A: Pays every hour at the regular rate
misconceptions.D: Pays every hour at the overtime rate

sources: U.S. Department of Labor: Under the FLSA, covered nonexempt employees receive overtime pay of at least 1.5 times the regular rate for hours over 40 in a workweek; some states set a higher minimum wage than the federal one. (https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime)

IRS (Publication 531): Employees who receive $20 or more in cash and charged tips in a month from one employer must report them to that employer; all tips, including noncash tips, are income. (https://www.irs.gov/publications/p531)

IRS (No tax on tips deduction): A new deduction for qualified tips (tax years 2025-2028, with limits) lowers income tax only; tips still must be reported, and Social Security and Medicare taxes still apply. (https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/what-the-no-tax-on-tips-deduction-means-for-you)

questions.prompt: Malik's pay stub shows "Gross pay: $882." What does gross pay mean?

choices.text: His total earnings before any deductions
The amount deposited into his bank account
His pay after taxes but before his retirement contribution
The overtime portion of his paycheck only

questions.correct_answer: His total earnings before any deductions
questions.intro: Paychecks show two key amounts. Gross pay is everything earned for the period. Net pay ("take-home pay") is what is left after deductions such as taxes and benefit costs, and it is what is actually deposited.
questions.feedback: Gross pay is the total earned before deductions; net pay is what he takes home.

misconceptions.B: Confuses gross pay with net pay
misconceptions.C: Thinks gross pay is partly after deductions

questions.prompt: How many hours is 7 hours and 15 minutes, written as a decimal?

choices.text: 7.15 hours
7.5 hours
7.75 hours
7.25 hours

questions.intro: An hour has 60 minutes. To change minutes to part of an hour, divide by 60: 15 ÷ 60 = 0.25.
questions.feedback: 15 minutes = 15/60 = 0.25 hour, so 7 h 15 min = 7.25 hours.

misconceptions.A: Writes minutes as hundredths of an hour
misconceptions.B: Treats 15 minutes as half an hour

questions.prompt: Jon works 10 hours a day, Monday through Thursday, and no other hours that week. Under the federal rule, how many overtime hours does he earn?

choices.text: 8 hours
2 hours
10 hours
0 hours

questions.intro: Federal overtime is based on hours in a WORKWEEK (any fixed, repeating 7-day period), not hours in a day. A few states also require daily overtime, so state law can add protection.
questions.feedback: 4 × 10 = 40 hours, which is not over 40 in the workweek, so there is no federal overtime. A state with daily overtime rules could require more.

misconceptions.C: Counts one whole day as overtime

questions.prompt: A salaried store manager meets the legal tests for an "exempt" employee and works 50 hours one week. What overtime pay does federal law require?

choices.text: No overtime pay is required
Time and a half for the 10 extra hours
Double time for every hour over 40
One extra day off for each hour over 40

questions.intro: Some salaried employees are "exempt" from overtime because they are paid at least a minimum salary and their main duties are executive, administrative, or professional. Being paid a salary alone does not make someone exempt; the duties test also matters.
questions.feedback: Exempt employees are not entitled to overtime pay under federal law, even for long weeks.

questions.prompt: Kai, a restaurant employee, received $410 in cash and card tips this month at one job. What does the IRS require?

choices.text: Nothing; tips are gifts and never taxed
He reports tips only in months when they exceed $1,000 in total
Nothing, because a tip deduction means tips are no longer reported
He reports them to his employer; they are taxable income

questions.correct_answer: He reports them to his employer; they are taxable income
questions.intro: Tips are taxable income. An employee who receives $20 or more in cash and charged (card) tips in a month at one job must report them to that employer, who includes them in payroll and withholding. Noncash tips (such as tickets) are not reported to the employer but are still income. A deduction for some qualified tips, available in recent tax years, can lower income tax, but tips must still be reported, and Social Security and Medicare taxes still apply.
questions.feedback: Monthly cash and card tips of $20 or more must be reported to the employer, and tips are taxable.

misconceptions.C: Confuses a possible income tax deduction with reporting

questions.prompt: Lia works in a state whose applicable minimum wage is $15.00 per hour and that allows a tip credit. She works 20 hours at a $5.00 cash wage and earns $150 in tips. Her wages plus tips must reach at least the minimum wage for those hours. How much must her employer add?
questions.intro: When an employer pays a lower cash wage and counts tips toward the minimum wage, the employer must make up the difference if wages plus tips fall below the applicable minimum wage for the hours worked. Minimum wages and tip-credit rules differ by state; the federal minimum is lower than many state minimums.
questions.feedback: Required: 20 × $15 = $300. She received $100 + $150 = $250. The employer must add $50.

misconceptions.C: Gives her tips as the amount owed

questions.prompt: Kai's tips vary from $250 to $500 a week. Which budgeting approach is safest?

choices.text: Plan around a lower weekly amount and save the extra
Plan around his best week ever

questions.feedback: With uneven income, budgeting on a conservative amount and saving surpluses smooths slow weeks.

misconceptions.C: Leaves no cushion for slow weeks
